summary:
As of 2026-10-10, Expo SDK 57 is the stable release (expo 57.0.27, React Native 0.86.3, React 19.2.3). SDK 58 is in beta under the npm `next` tag, at 58.0.7 on React Native 0.88.0-rc.4. Expo says the store builds of Expo Go will move to SDK 58 shortly after it goes stable and will then drop SDK 57. So build on SDK 57 with development builds, and plan the SDK 58 upgrade after it is stable.

expo-haptics 57.0.3 gives only preset feedback: 5 impact styles, 3 notification types, selection, and 19 Android system constants. It has no custom patterns. On Android, `impactAsync` drives a basic Vibrator waveform. `performAndroidHapticsAsync` uses the system's haptic feedback instead, but it only works from 57.0.2 onwards, and several constants need Android API 30 or 34.

For custom patterns, add react-native-pulsar 1.7.0, which Expo's own haptics page recommends. It needs a development build, has no web support, and crashes on import in Expo Go, so it must sit behind a fallback wrapper.

`npx expo start --web` renders an expo-router app. I confirmed this on this Windows machine by exporting the existing mobile/ app for web and loading it in a browser.

Store rules: Google Play requires API 36 for new apps and updates since 2026-08-31. Apple requires Xcode 26 and the iOS 26 SDK since 2026-04-28. Apple ignores the Liquid Glass opt-out key when you build with the iOS 27 SDK.

All 24 font packages exist on npm.

findings.claim: Expo SDK 57 is the latest stable SDK (expo 57.0.27, npm tag `latest`). SDK 58 is in beta as expo 58.0.7 under the `next` tag. SDK 58 bundles react-native 0.88.0-rc.4 and React 19.3.0.
findings.evidence: Running `npm view expo dist-tags` on 2026-10-10 returned latest 57.0.27 and next 58.0.7. The SDK 58 beta post (2026-09-15) says the beta lasts 3–4 weeks. Comparing bundledNativeModules for 58.0.7 against 57.0.27 shows react-native 0.88.0-rc.4.

findings.claim: SDK 57 compatible versions: react 19.2.3, react-dom 19.2.3, react-native 0.86.3, react-native-web ~0.21.0 (latest match 0.21.4), expo-router ~57.0.25, reanimated 4.5.1, worklets 0.10.1 (required), gesture-handler ~2.32.0, safe-area-context ~5.7.0, screens ~4.26.0 (4.26.2), svg 15.15.4, expo-haptics ~57.0.3, expo-camera ~57.0.6, expo-image-picker ~57.0.20, expo-local-authentication ~57.0.3, expo-secure-store ~57.0.4, expo-blur ~57.0.3, expo-linear-gradient ~57.0.2, expo-glass-effect ~57.0.4, expo-font ~57.0.4, expo-image ~57.0.5, expo-audio ~57.0.5, expo-constants ~57.0.21, expo-linking ~57.0.12, expo-status-bar ~57.0.1, expo-splash-screen ~57.0.9, expo-system-ui ~57.0.4, expo-symbols ~57.0.3, @expo/vector-icons ^15.0.2 (15.1.1), async-storage 2.2.0.
findings.evidence: Read directly from expo@57.0.27/bundledNativeModules.json. Each range was resolved with `npm view <pkg>@<range> version`. reanimated 4.5.1 declares peer dependencies react-native '0.83 - 0.86' and react-native-worklets '0.10.x'. The npm `latest` tags are newer than these pins (reanimated 4.7.1, gesture-handler 3.3.0, async-storage 3.1.1), so install with `npx expo install`, not plain npm.

findings.claim: `create-expo-app` (default template expo-template-default@57.0.29) produces an expo-router app in `src/app`. It uses NativeTabs from `expo-router/unstable-native-tabs`, with `.web.tsx` headless-tab fallbacks. Typed routes and the React Compiler are on, `predictiveBackGestureEnabled` is false, and the iOS icon is an Icon Composer `.icon` file.
findings.evidence: I downloaded the tarball. Its dependencies are @expo/ui, expo, expo-constants, expo-device, expo-font, expo-glass-effect, expo-image, expo-linking, expo-router, expo-splash-screen, expo-status-bar, expo-symbols, expo-system-ui, expo-web-browser, react, react-dom, react-native, gesture-handler, reanimated, safe-area-context, screens, react-native-web and worklets. devDependencies are @types/react ~19.2.2 and typescript ~6.0.3. It does not include react-native-svg, @expo/vector-icons, expo-haptics or expo-dev-client.

findings.claim: expo-haptics 57.0.3 API surface: notificationAsync(NotificationFeedbackType Success|Warning|Error), impactAsync(ImpactFeedbackStyle Light|Medium|Heavy|Soft|Rigid), selectionAsync(), and performAndroidHapticsAsync(AndroidHaptics) with 19 values. The values are Confirm, Reject, Gesture_Start, Gesture_End, Toggle_On, Toggle_Off, Clock_Tick, Context_Click, Drag_Start, Keyboard_Tap, Keyboard_Press, Keyboard_Release, Long_Press, Virtual_Key, Virtual_Key_Release, No_Haptics, Segment_Tick, Segment_Frequent_Tick and Text_Handle_Move. There is no custom-pattern or intensity API.
findings.evidence: From the package source (src/Haptics.types.ts and src/Haptics.ts). On iOS it calls UIImpact, UINotification and UISelection FeedbackGenerators with no intensity parameter. On Android, impact, notification and selection use Vibrator.createWaveform with amplitudes of 30–70 out of 255. performAndroidHapticsAsync calls View.performHapticFeedback on the main thread, a fix made in 57.0.2 (2026-08-26); before that it did nothing. Constants missing on the device throw HapticsNotSupportedException.

findings.claim: The AndroidHaptics constants need these minimum API levels. CONFIRM, REJECT, GESTURE_START and GESTURE_END need API 30. TOGGLE_ON, TOGGLE_OFF, DRAG_START, SEGMENT_TICK, SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK and NO_HAPTICS need API 34. KEYBOARD_PRESS, KEYBOARD_RELEASE, TEXT_HANDLE_MOVE and VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE need API 27. CLOCK_TICK needs 21, CONTEXT_CLICK 23, KEYBOARD_TAP 8, VIRTUAL_KEY 5 and LONG_PRESS 3. SDK 57 supports Android 7 (API 24) and up, so these calls need an API-level guard and a fallback.
findings.evidence: I read the 'Added in API level' value for each constant on Android's HapticFeedbackConstants reference page. The Expo SDK 57 version table lists Android 7+ with compile and target SDK 36.

findings.claim: Web and iOS caveats for expo-haptics. On web it uses navigator.vibrate, and on iOS Safari it falls back to a hidden checkbox switch trick. performAndroidHapticsAsync does nothing off Android. On iOS, the Taptic Engine is silent in Low Power Mode, when the user has turned off haptics, while the camera is active, and during dictation.
findings.evidence: The web implementation is in src/ExpoHaptics.web.ts. Expo's haptics docs list the conditions under which iOS stays silent. Because haptics are silent while the camera is active, the receipt-capture screen needs visual confirmation and cannot rely on a haptic.

findings.claim: react-native-pulsar 1.7.0, from Software Mansion, is the best-maintained library for custom cross-platform patterns. Expo's own haptics page recommends it for advanced haptics.
findings.evidence: Published 2026-08-11 with 110,984 weekly downloads (Oct 2–8). It is a TurboModule (codegenConfig RNPulsarSpec) and requires react-native-worklets. It offers about 200 named Presets plus System.* presets, and usePatternComposer with discrete events and amplitude/frequency envelopes (time in ms, values 0–1). It also offers useRealtimeComposer.set(amplitude, frequency), useAdaptiveHaptics({ios, android}), and Settings.enableHaptics/getHapticsSupportLevel. iOS uses the PulsarHaptics pod 1.4.0 (Core Haptics). Android uses com.swmansion:pulsar 1.3.0; per its docs, primitives need API 30+ and envelopes need API 36+. The 1.7.0 tarball has no app.plugin.js and no web build, and it calls TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing at import.

findings.claim: react-native-haptic-feedback 3.0.0 is the most downloaded alternative (484,149 a week). It supports AHAP files and intensity, but its Android pattern playback is amplitude-only, and AHAP files need extra native bundling under Expo CNG.
findings.evidence: Its triggerPattern on Android builds VibrationEffect.createWaveform from the intensity of each event (VibrateFactory.vibratePattern), not a Composition. playAHAP is iOS-only and expects the file in the app bundle. Its app.plugin.js does nothing, so .ahap files would need a custom config plugin. Last published 2026-03-29.

findings.claim: The other candidates are niche, stale or iOS-only. expo-ahap 0.0.1 (2023, iOS only, 3,370 a week). @candlefinance/haptics 0.3.3 (2024, 154 a week). react-native-core-haptics-api 0.1.2 (2022, 27 a week). react-native-nitro-haptics 0.2.3, a drop-in for expo-haptics on Nitro with no patterns (7,384 a week). @renegades/react-native-tickle 0.1.2, AHAP-style on Nitro and iOS-only (6,394 a week). react-native-hapticlabs 0.11.0, which plays AHAP/HLA/OGG files from Hapticlabs Studio (7,804 a week). @mhpdev/react-native-haptics 1.1.1, New Architecture only (2,480 a week). react-native-turbo-haptics 1.2.0 (1,060 a week).
findings.evidence: I took versions and dates from `npm view <pkg> version time.modified`, downloads from api.npmjs.org for 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-08, and capabilities from each package's README and native sources.

findings.claim: The App Store Expo Go supports SDK 57 and requires an Expo login in both the CLI and the iOS app. Expo has said the store versions will move to SDK 58 soon after it is stable, which drops SDK 57.
findings.evidence: The 2026-09-03 changelog says the App Store Expo Go now supports SDK 57 and requires login. The SDK 58 beta post says the store versions update shortly after the stable release, before they drop SDK 57. The May 2026 post says `eas go` builds Expo Go for your own TestFlight and needs an Apple Developer Program membership.

findings.claim: Expo Go cannot test these Vaultwise needs, so they require a development build: Face ID on iOS, SecureStore `requireAuthentication` when biometrics are present, fonts embedded through the expo-font plugin, `android.blockedPermissions`, a faithful splash screen, and any third-party native module (Pulsar).
findings.evidence: The LocalAuthentication docs say Face ID is not supported in Expo Go. The SecureStore docs say `requireAuthentication` is unsupported in Expo Go because NSFaceIDUsageDescription is missing. The fonts guide says the config plugin does not work with Expo Go. The app config docs say blockedPermissions is not available in Expo Go. The splash-screen docs say Expo Go shows the app icon instead of the splash screen. Pulsar is not in bundledNativeModules.

findings.claim: `npx expo start --web` and `npx expo export --platform web` render an expo-router app on Windows. I confirmed this locally.
findings.evidence: I ran `npx expo export --platform web` in C:/Users/shaik/VaultWise/mobile (expo 57, router 57.0.25, Node 24.11.1) to a scratch directory, served it on 127.0.0.1 and opened it in the browser pane. The template home screen rendered. The web bundle is 2.1 MB, and expo-symbols pulls in the Material Symbols font (971 KB). On web, expo-secure-store is an empty stub, so calls throw. expo-local-authentication reports no hardware, GlassView falls back to a plain View, and NativeTabs falls back to a basic web tab bar.

findings.claim: Google Play: since 2026-08-31, new apps and updates must target API 36 (Android 16). An extension to 2026-11-01 can be requested. SDK 57 already targets and compiles against 36.
findings.evidence: Google's target-SDK page gives these dates. Expo's version table lists targetSdkVersion 36 for SDK 57.

findings.claim: Apple: since 2026-04-28, uploads must be built with Xcode 26+ against the iOS 26 SDK. Since 2026-09-09, the minimum deployment target is iOS 13. Apple's requirements page does not yet mention an iOS 27 SDK requirement. SDK 57 needs Xcode 26.4+ and supports iOS 16.4+.
findings.evidence: Apple's upcoming-requirements page and Expo's version table.

findings.claim: Liquid Glass: standard system components (bars, tab bars, sheets, controls) adopt it automatically when the app is built with the latest SDK. The UIDesignRequiresCompatibility opt-out is temporary, and the system ignores it for apps built for iOS 27 or later. SDK 57 builds with Xcode 27 only if you opt in to scene support through expo-build-properties `ios.enableSceneSupport` (expo@57.0.23+). SDK 58 uses the scene lifecycle by default.
findings.evidence: Apple's 'Adopting Liquid Glass' page and the UIDesignRequiresCompatibility reference (read from Apple's docs JSON). The SDK 57 changelog section on building with Xcode 27. The expo-build-properties 57.0.22 type definitions.

findings.claim: Native tabs (the iOS 26 Liquid Glass tab bar) allow at most 5 tabs on Android. The tab bar height cannot be measured, all tab screens render eagerly, and FlatList support is limited. The import path is `expo-router/unstable-native-tabs` in SDK 54–57 and `expo-router/native-tabs` (stable) in SDK 58. The planned tabs (Home, Vaults, Emergency, Invest, More) fit exactly within the 5-tab limit.
findings.evidence: From the 'Known limitations' section of the Expo Router native tabs docs and the SDK 58 beta notes.

findings.claim: Android 16 rules for apps targeting API 36: edge-to-edge cannot be turned off, predictive back animations are on by default (onBackPressed and KEYCODE_BACK are no longer delivered unless the app opts out with enableOnBackInvokedCallback=false), and orientation and resizability locks are ignored on screens 600dp or wider. Expo removed `newArchEnabled` from app.json in SDK 55 and `edgeToEdgeEnabled` in SDK 55. `android.predictiveBackGestureEnabled` defaults to false, which sets enableOnBackInvokedCallback.
findings.evidence: Android 16 behaviour-changes page. The SDK 55 changelog. The SDK 57 app config reference. The SDK 57 ExpoConfig types contain no newArchEnabled or edgeToEdgeEnabled.

findings.claim: Account deletion: both stores require deletion to start inside the app. Google Play also requires a web deletion link declared in the Data safety form. Regulated industries may add verification or customer-service steps (Apple guideline 5.1.1(ix)), and Google allows keeping data for regulatory reasons if this is disclosed.
findings.evidence: Apple's support page on offering account deletion and Google Play Help article 13327111.

findings.claim: Privacy manifest: the Required Reason API rule has applied to uploads since 2024-05-01. Expo writes `ios.privacyManifests` into PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy. The packages installed today declare UserDefaults CA92.1, FileTimestamp C617.1/0A2A.1/3B52.1, SystemBootTime 35F9.1 and DiskSpace E174.1/85F4.1.
findings.evidence: Apple's requirements page and Expo's privacy guide. I scanned all PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy files in mobile/node_modules (react-native, expo-constants, expo-device, expo-file-system, expo-system-ui).

findings.claim: The Play photo-permission policy is satisfied. expo-image-picker uses the system Photo Picker and does not declare READ_MEDIA_IMAGES. Setting `microphonePermission:false` in the plugin blocks RECORD_AUDIO. Setting `cameraPermission:false` in the image-picker plugin would block CAMERA for expo-camera too, so do not set it to false.
findings.evidence: From the expo-image-picker AndroidManifest.xml and plugin source (withBlockedPermissions), and Google Play Help article 14115180. Full compliance became mandatory on 2025-05-28.

findings.claim: All 24 requested @expo-google-fonts packages exist. Each one is a set of static TTFs, one per weight (about 91 KB each), with a matching subpath import (for example `@expo-google-fonts/geist/400Regular`). Each works with expo-font's useFonts. Variable-font support in expo-font arrives in SDK 58.
findings.evidence: From `npm view` and the package index.d.ts files. The Expo fonts guide covers the useFonts and config-plugin paths, and the SDK 58 beta notes add variable fonts.

findings.claim: Repo state: a `mobile/` Expo SDK 57 project already exists in the working tree but is uncommitted. The root tsconfig excludes it, ESLint and Vitest ignore it, and next.config.ts allows CORS from the Expo web dev server at localhost:8081. Metro's server root resolves to mobile/ because the root package.json has no `workspaces`.
findings.evidence: From `git status` and `git diff`, plus running `require('@expo/config/paths').getMetroServerRoot()` inside mobile/, which printed C:\Users\shaik\VaultWise\mobile.

findings.claim: Recommendation (my inference): use expo-haptics behind a semantic wrapper in Expo Go and on web. Add react-native-pulsar 1.7.0 only in development builds, loaded lazily after checking that the RNPulsar module exists. Build a small local Expo module only if Pulsar fails on RN 0.86 or 0.88, or if designers must ship .ahap files verbatim.
findings.evidence: Pulsar's development dependencies were tested against RN 0.81.1 and worklets 0.7.2, with peer dependencies of '*'. Compatibility with RN 0.86.3 and worklets 0.10.1 is unverified and needs a one-day spike.

spec:
# Vaultwise mobile: engineering stack spec (Expo SDK 57, checked 2026-10-10)

Facts below cite primary sources. Lines marked **(inference)** are my recommendations, not documented facts.

Raw evidence is saved in `C:/Users/shaik/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-shaik-VaultWise/9e11eaa3-37f8-4e12-90a3-5e69f6c8b8c9/scratchpad/research/stack/`:
- `raw/` holds bundledNativeModules for SDK 57 and 58, the template, the haptics libraries, and the docs pages as .md files.
- `versions-sdk57.json` has the resolved versions.

---

## 0. Decision: SDK 57 now, SDK 58 after it is stable

| | SDK 57 (`latest`) | SDK 58 (`next`, beta) |
|---|---|---|
| expo | 57.0.27 (2026-10-06) | 58.0.7 (2026-10-09) |
| React Native / React | 0.86.3 / 19.2.3 | 0.88.0-rc.4 / 19.3.0 |
| Store Expo Go | Supports 57 today (iOS needs a login) | Arrives "shortly after stable"; the store app then drops SDK 57 |
| Notable changes | none | Strict TS API by default, `expo-router/native-tabs` becomes stable (new import path), R8 on by default, iOS scene lifecycle, variable fonts, `File.write` becomes async |

Sources: https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-57, https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-58-beta, `npm view expo dist-tags`.

**Recommendation (inference):**
- Build on SDK 57 now; the existing `mobile/` scaffold already uses it.
- Make the development build (expo-dev-client) the main dev loop.
- Use store Expo Go only for quick demos until it moves to SDK 58.
- Budget about a day to upgrade to SDK 58 once RN 0.88 is final: `npx expo install expo@^58 --fix`, then follow the router SDK 57→58 migration guide.

---

## 1. Versions (SDK 57, from `expo@57.0.27/bundledNativeModules.json`)

**Rule:** always add packages with `npx expo install <pkg>` from inside `mobile/`; it picks the SDK-pinned version. Run `npx expo-doctor@latest` before each build.

**Default template** (`npx create-expo-app@latest --template default`, which installs expo-template-default@57.0.29, published 2026-10-09):

- Dependencies:
  - Expo modules: @expo/ui, expo, expo-constants, expo-device, expo-font, expo-glass-effect, expo-image, expo-linking, expo-router, expo-splash-screen, expo-status-bar, expo-symbols, expo-system-ui, expo-web-browser.
  - React and React Native: react, react-dom, react-native, react-native-gesture-handler, react-native-reanimated, react-native-safe-area-context, react-native-screens, react-native-web, react-native-worklets.
- devDependencies: @types/react ~19.2.2 and typescript ~6.0.3.
- Structure: `src/app/{_layout,index,explore}.tsx`. NativeTabs comes from `expo-router/unstable-native-tabs`, with `app-tabs.web.tsx` providing headless tabs on web.
- app.json: `experiments.typedRoutes` and `experiments.reactCompiler` are true, `android.predictiveBackGestureEnabled` is false, `ios.icon` points to an Icon Composer `.icon` file, and `web.output` is `static`.
- Not included: react-native-svg, @expo/vector-icons, expo-haptics, expo-dev-client.

---

## 2. expo-haptics 57.0.3: full API

Source: https://unpkg.com/expo-haptics@57.0.3/src/

| Function | iOS | Android | Web |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notificationAsync(type = Success)`. Types: `Success`, `Warning`, `Error` | UINotificationFeedbackGenerator | Vibrator waveform | navigator.vibrate: [40,100,40], [50,100,50], [60,100,60,100,60]. iOS Safari: 2–3 switch "clicks" |
| `impactAsync(style = Medium)`. Styles: `Light`, `Medium`, `Heavy`, `Soft`, `Rigid` | UIImpactFeedbackGenerator (no intensity parameter) | Vibrator `createWaveform`, 43–60 ms at amplitudes 30, 50 or 70 out of 255. Requires VIBRATE, which is added automatically | vibrate 35–60 ms |
| `selectionAsync()` | UISelectionFeedbackGenerator | Vibrator waveform | vibrate 50 ms |
| `performAndroidHapticsAsync(AndroidHaptics)` | does nothing | `View.performHapticFeedback` (system-tuned). **Broken before 57.0.2**, fixed 2026-08-26 | does nothing |

**AndroidHaptics values and minimum Android API** (from developer.android.com/reference/android/view/HapticFeedbackConstants):

| Value | Minimum API |
|---|---|
| `Confirm` | 30 |
| `Reject` | 30 |
| `Gesture_Start`, `Gesture_End` | 30 |
| `Toggle_On`, `Toggle_Off` | 34 |
| `Clock_Tick` | 21 |
| `Context_Click` | 23 |
| `Drag_Start` | 34 |
| `Keyboard_Tap` | 8 |
| `Keyboard_Press`, `Keyboard_Release` | 27 |
| `Long_Press` | 3 |
| `Virtual_Key` | 5 |
| `Virtual_Key_Release` | 27 |
| `No_Haptics` | 34 |
| `Segment_Tick`, `Segment_Frequent_Tick` | 34 |
| `Text_Handle_Move` | 27 |

On older devices, a constant the device lacks throws `HapticsNotSupportedException`. Guard each call with `Platform.Version` and wrap it in try/catch.

**No custom-pattern or intensity API exists.** Expo's docs point to Pulsar for that.

iOS stays silent in these cases (Expo docs): Low Power Mode, haptics turned off in system settings, **camera active**, dictation active. The receipt-capture screen therefore needs visual confirmation.

### Semantic mapping (API choice is inference; event semantics come from the enum docs)

| Vaultwise event | iOS | Android (API ≥ min, else fallback) |
|---|---|---|
| Tab switch, segmented control | `selectionAsync()` | `Segment_Tick` (34), else `Clock_Tick` |
| PIN digit | `impactAsync(Light)` | `Keyboard_Tap` |
| PIN accepted, Face ID ok, payment approved | `notificationAsync(Success)` | `Confirm` (30), else `Long_Press` |
| Wrong PIN, payment declined | `notificationAsync(Error)` | `Reject` (30), else `notificationAsync(Error)` |
| Over-limit warning, guardrail | `notificationAsync(Warning)` | `notificationAsync(Warning)` |
| Toggle (round-ups, rules) | `impactAsync(Light)` | `Toggle_On` / `Toggle_Off` (34), else `Clock_Tick` |
| Long-press vault card | `impactAsync(Medium)` | `Long_Press` |
| Reorder drag start | `impactAsync(Soft)` | `Drag_Start` (34), else `Long_Press` |
| Amount slider step | `selectionAsync()` (throttled) | `Segment_Frequent_Tick` (34), else `Clock_Tick` |
| Emergency Tier 2 hold-to-release | Pulsar realtime ramp (dev build); else repeat `impactAsync(Rigid)` | same |

---

## 3. Custom haptic patterns: libraries compared

Weekly downloads are for 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-08, from api.npmjs.org.

| Package | Latest (publish date) | Downloads/wk | Architecture | Expo | Pattern API | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **react-native-pulsar** | 1.7.0 (2026-08-11) | 110,984 | TurboModule (codegen), New Arch; peer `react-native-worklets` | Dev build only. No config plugin in 1.7.0; autolinks via prebuild | About 200 named presets plus System.*. `usePatternComposer({discretePattern:[{time,amplitude,frequency}], continuousPattern:{amplitude:[{time,value}],frequency:[…]}})` with time in ms and values 0–1. Also `useRealtimeComposer().set(a,f)`, `useAdaptiveHaptics({ios,android})`, `Settings.enableHaptics/getHapticsSupportLevel`. Callable from worklets. iOS uses Core Haptics (PulsarHaptics pod 1.4.0). ### Recommendation

**(a) Expo Go:** use `expo-haptics` only, through the wrapper below. On Android, prefer `performAndroidHapticsAsync` with an API guard. It is system-tuned, and the library's own JSDoc recommends it over Vibrator.

**(b) Development build:** add `react-native-pulsar@1.7.0` for 3–5 signature moments, such as vault unlock, Pay with Vaultwise approved, the Emergency hold-to-release ramp, and a round-up "coin drop".

Why Pulsar:
- Expo's haptics page recommends it.
- Its maintainer also ships Reanimated, Worklets and Gesture Handler, which are already in this stack.
- It is the only active library with true cross-platform amplitude/frequency patterns plus Android primitives and envelopes.
- Its worklet API pairs with gesture-driven haptics.

Risk: Pulsar was developed and tested against RN 0.81.1 and worklets 0.7.2, and its peer dependencies are `*`. Validate it on RN 0.86.3 with worklets 0.10.1 in a one-day dev-build spike **(inference)**.

**(c) Local Expo module** (`npx create-expo-module@latest --local`): **not now (inference).** Use it only if Pulsar fails, or if designers must ship `.ahap` files verbatim. In that case, write about 150–250 lines: Swift `CHHapticEngine` + `CHHapticPattern(dictionary:)`, and Kotlin `VibrationEffect.startComposition()` (API 30+) falling back to `createWaveform`. Add a config plugin that copies `.ahap` files into the iOS bundle.

### Haptics wrapper (inference; required because Pulsar throws at import when its module is absent)

```
src/lib/haptics/
  index.ts           // semantic API: tap(), select(), success(), warning(), error(), pinDigit(), toggle(on), longPress(), sliderTick(), signature(name)
  engine.native.ts   // expo-haptics + Android API guards; lazy Pulsar
  engine.web.ts      // expo-haptics web (vibrate / iOS Safari switch) or no-op
  patterns.ts        // Pulsar Pattern objects (ms, 0..1)
```

```ts
// engine.native.ts (sketch)
import { Platform, TurboModuleRegistry } from 'react-native';
import * as H from 'expo-haptics';
const pulsar = TurboModuleRegistry.get('RNPulsar') ? require('react-native-pulsar') : null; // null in Expo Go
const api = Platform.OS === 'android' ? (Platform.Version as number) : 0;
export async function confirm() {
  if (Platform.OS === 'android' && api >= 30) { try { return await H.performAndroidHapticsAsync(H.AndroidHaptics.Confirm); } catch {} }
  return H.notificationAsync(H.NotificationFeedbackType.Success);
}
```

Also:
- Keep a global in-app "Haptics" toggle, persisted with AsyncStorage, that short-circuits every call.
- Throttle slider ticks to at most one per 40–60 ms.

## 4. Expo Go, development builds and web preview on Windows

- **Store Expo Go currently runs SDK 57.**
  - On iOS you must log in to the same Expo account in both `npx expo login` and the Expo Go app (2026-09-03).
  - Expo Go can only load EAS Update projects you own.
  - The store apps will move to SDK 58 soon after it is stable, and will then drop 57.
  - After that, Android devices and emulators still get SDK 57 Expo Go via Expo CLI or expo.dev/go.
  - iOS devices need `eas go`, which requires an Apple Developer Program membership.
- **Works in Expo Go:** all Expo SDK modules in the table above, plus Reanimated, Gesture Handler, SVG, AsyncStorage, Google Fonts via `useFonts`, expo-glass-effect, expo-blur and expo-mesh-gradient.
- **Needs a development build:**
  - Pulsar or any other third-party native module.
  - **Face ID**.
  - SecureStore `requireAuthentication` on a device with biometrics.
  - Fonts embedded through the expo-font plugin.
  - `android.blockedPermissions`.
  - A faithful splash screen.
  - Custom scheme and universal or app links.
  - Real permission strings and icons.
- **Windows:**
  - There is no iOS Simulator.
  - iOS: use store Expo Go on an iPhone now, or an EAS cloud dev build (`eas build -p ios --profile development`; needs an Apple Developer account).
  - Android: run the Android Studio emulator with `npx expo run:android`, or use an EAS build.
- **Web preview works.** I confirmed it on this machine: `npx expo export --platform web` in `mobile/` produced a 2.1 MB bundle that rendered in a browser. `npx expo start --web` (port 8081) is the dev equivalent, and next.config.ts already allows CORS for `http://localhost:8081`.
- **Web caveats** (these need `.web.ts` shims):
  - `expo-secure-store`'s web module is an empty stub, so calls throw. Use a sessionStorage or in-memory shim for preview only.
  - `expo-local-authentication` returns no hardware, so skip the biometric step on web.
  - `GlassView` becomes a plain `View`.
  - NativeTabs falls back to a basic web tab bar. Keep the template's `app-tabs.web.tsx` pattern.
  - Pulsar is native only.
  - expo-camera on web uses getUserMedia, which needs localhost or https.
  - expo-symbols on web downloads the Material Symbols font (971 KB).
  - Keep `web.output: "single"`. `static` pre-renders every route in Node and breaks on native-only modules **(inference)**.

### 5a. Liquid Glass for this app (my inference from Apple and Expo docs)

- `NativeTabs` renders the real UITabBar. On iOS 26 that is the floating Liquid Glass bar, with `minimizeBehavior="onScrollDown"` and SF Symbol icons. On Android it is Material 3.
- Native tabs limits:
  - Maximum of 5 tabs on Android. The plan (Home, Vaults, Emergency, Invest, More) fits exactly.
  - Styling is limited.
  - No raised custom "Emergency" button.
  - The tab bar height cannot be measured.
  - All tabs mount eagerly.
- The Gen Z visual identity should live in content: cards, gradients, mesh gradients, type and motion. It should not live in the iOS tab bar chrome.
- Use `GlassView` (`expo-glass-effect`) sparingly, for 1–2 hero surfaces:
  - Gate it on `isLiquidGlassAvailable()`.
  - Respect `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceTransparencyEnabled()`.
  - Never animate its `opacity` to 0; use `glassEffectStyle` animation instead.
  - Provide a solid or `expo-blur` fallback for Android and web.
- If design insists on a fully custom tab bar, use JS tabs or headless `expo-router/ui` tabs with your own GlassView background. This gives full control but loses the system Liquid Glass behaviour.
- The app icon should be an Icon Composer `.icon` file, as `ios.icon` already is.

```tsx
import { useFonts } from 'expo-font';
import * as SplashScreen from 'expo-splash-screen';
import { BricolageGrotesque_700Bold } from '@expo-google-fonts/bricolage-grotesque/700Bold';

import { GeistMono_500Medium } from '@expo-google-fonts/geist-mono/500Medium';
SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync();
const [loaded, error] = useFonts({ BricolageGrotesque_700Bold, Geist_400Regular, GeistMono_500Medium });
useEffect(() => { if (loaded || error) SplashScreen.hideAsync(); }, [loaded, error]);
// <Text style={{ fontFamily: 'BricolageGrotesque_700Bold' }} />
```

**Production option: embed the fonts.** This needs a dev build and is native only. Add the files to the `expo-font` plugin, e.g. `"fonts": ["node_modules/@expo-google-fonts/bricolage-grotesque/700Bold/BricolageGrotesque_700Bold.ttf"]`.

After embedding, the family name differs by platform:
- Android uses the file name (`BricolageGrotesque_700Bold`).
- iOS uses the PostScript name.
- Use `Platform.select` to pick the right one, and keep `useFonts` for web.

**(inference)** Limit the app to 3–5 font faces.

## 8. Gotchas: Windows, and living inside the Next.js repo

1. **Keep `mobile/` a nested, independent project.**
   - It has its own package.json, lockfile and node_modules.
   - Do NOT add `workspaces` to the root package.json. The root has react 19.2.8 for Next 16.3.8, while SDK 57 pins react 19.2.3. Expo's docs say duplicate React versions in one app cause runtime errors.
   - Without workspaces, Metro's server root is `mobile/`. I verified this, and it means no `metro.config.js` is needed.
2. **Isolation already in the working tree (uncommitted):**
   - Root `tsconfig.json` has `"exclude": ["node_modules","mobile"]`.
   - `eslint.config.mjs` ignores `mobile/**`.
   - `vitest.config.mts` excludes `mobile/**`.
   - `next.config.ts` sends dev-only CORS headers for `http://localhost:8081`.
   - Commit these together with `mobile/`.
3. **Tailwind v4 scans the whole repo** except files in .gitignore and node_modules. Add `@source not "../../mobile";` to `src/app/globals.css` so RN class-like strings don't bloat the web CSS **(inference; syntax per tailwindcss.com)**.
4. **Sharing types with the API.** Metro only watches `mobile/`, so importing from `../src` breaks. Generate or copy zod schemas and types into `mobile/src/lib/api/` instead **(inference)**.
5. **Run every Expo command from `mobile/`**: `npx expo …`, `npx expo install`, `npx expo-doctor`. Never run `npm install` at the root for mobile packages.
6. **Path aliases.** Both projects use `@/*` pointing at their own `src`. That is fine because the tsconfigs are separate; VS Code picks the nearest tsconfig.
7. **Reaching the API from devices:**
   - A phone cannot reach your PC's `localhost:3000`. Use the PC's LAN IP; the Android emulator uses `10.0.2.2`. Run `next dev -H 0.0.0.0` **(inference)**.
   - Dev builds allow cleartext HTTP: the template's debug manifest sets `usesCleartextTraffic=true`, and iOS ATS sets `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`.
   - **Release and preview builds need HTTPS.**
   - Put the base URL in `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL`.
8. **Node.** SDK 57 needs Node ≥22.13 and SDK 58 needs 22.13+, 24.3+ or 26+, with no odd-numbered releases. This machine runs 24.11.1 ✔.
9. **Windows Android native builds** compile C++ (New Arch). Keep the repo path short (current path is fine) and enable Win32 long paths if CMake or ninja path errors appear **(inference)**. iOS builds must go through EAS.
10. **Expo Go's iOS login requirement.** Teammates must sign in to the same Expo account in both the CLI and the app, or share a dev build via EAS internal distribution.
11. **Version drift.** npm `latest` for reanimated, gesture-handler, screens, async-storage and others is newer than SDK 57 supports. A stray `npm i` breaks native builds; use `npx expo install --fix`.
12. **SecureStore and biometrics.**
    - Values stored with `requireAuthentication` become unreadable when biometric enrolment changes.
    - On iOS, keychain values survive an uninstall and reinstall.
    - Reads with `requireAuthentication` block the JS thread.

13. **Haptics and camera.** iOS haptics are silent while the camera runs. Pulsar must sit behind the wrapper, or web and Expo Go will crash at import.
